subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@finsecure.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Data isolation discussion (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few clarifying questions to make sure we scope the right deployment option for FinSecure. High level notes from our call:

- Primary concern: strict data isolation and control over keys/auditability.
- Considering: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, Redwood-managed control plane) vs Private VPC (customer-managed networking, option for private control plane/on-prem later).
- Security team wants clarity on: physical/compute isolation, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, retention, and network egress controls.

To help us recommend the right path, a few targeted questions we discussed — can you confirm the answers (or add details) when you have a moment?

1) Isolation requirements
   - Must tenant compute be fully single-tenant (no co-located containers/VMs for other customers), or is logical isolation (dedicated capacity) acceptable?
   - Do you require an on-prem option or is a Private VPC (dedicated VPC with customer-managed control plane) sufficient?

2) Key management and encryption
   - Is customer-managed KMS/HSM required for model artifacts and request logs? If yes, which provider (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM vendor)?

3) Network and data flow
   - Does all inference traffic need to stay within your VPC/VNet (no egress to public internet)? Any mandatory proxy/inspection appliance?
   - Are there strict egress IP allowlists we must adhere to?

4) Auditability and retention
   - Required retention window for request/response logs and audit trails? Any regulatory minima?

5) Timeline & procurement
   - When does security review complete? Any procurement/contract milestones we should align with?

Next steps I propose:
- I can loop in Vivek (solutions engineering) for a technical deep-dive to map a Private VPC architecture vs Dedicated capacity tradeoffs.
- I attached a short one-pager that compares Dedicated vs Private VPC at a glance and a network-reqs template (we'll fill together) to capture your VPC/KMS details.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-onepager.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

Available next week for a 45–60 minute technical session. A few slots I have: Tue 01/12 10:30–11:30 PT, Wed 01/13 09:00–10:00 PT, Thu 01/14 15:00–16:00 PT. Let me know what works for you and I’ll send an invite.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Onward: Vivek (SE) and Monica (Solutions) are cc’d to help scope the technical ask.
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinSecure Security <security@finsecure.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 18:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data isolation discussion (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the one-pager. Quick answers from our side to help you and your team:

- Preferred deployment: Private VPC with customer-managed control plane. Our security policy requires that production model inference runs in a VPC we control and that no customer compute is co-located with other tenants.

- Key management: Customer-managed KMS is required. We use AWS KMS with a dedicated key policy; long-term we'll look at an HSM-backed key (Thales/Entrust) for certain workloads.

- Network/data flow: All traffic must originate/terminate inside our VPC. No egress to public internet for payloads. We have an inline inspection appliance that will sit in front of the inference endpoints.

- Audit/retention: We need immutable audit logs for at least 3 years and the ability to export logs to our SIEM.

- Compliance: SOC 2 plus additional internal controls. We’ll need evidence of the following for your Private VPC offering:
   - Proof that control plane separation exists (diagram + description)
   - Confirmation that compute nodes for our VPC are not shared with other customers
   - KMS/HSM integration details and key life-cycle controls
   - Audit log schema and export options

Procurement timeline: Security team will review the one-pager this week (target sign-off by end of next week). Procurement expects to start contract discussions in mid-February.

Next steps from our side: I’ve cc’d security@finsecure.com to make it easier for your team to share the architecture details they need. Please propose times for the technical deep-dive and attach the network template you mentioned.

Thanks,

Alice Johnson
Head of Product Security, FinSecure
alice.johnson@finsecure.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data isolation discussion (Dedicated vs Private VPC) — tech deep-dive proposals

Alice / Security team —

Thanks for the quick responses and for looping in security. Vivek and I reviewed your notes and we’re aligned that Private VPC is the right next step given the customer-managed KMS and no-egress requirement. A couple of clarifying points before we lock the agenda for the technical deep-dive:

- Compute isolation: we need to confirm whether your requirement is for physically dedicated hosts (bare metal) or whether logical single-tenant (dedicated GPU pools where instances are not shared at the hypervisor level) is sufficient. Vivek — can you confirm the options we can offer and the delta on lead time/cost?

- KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS with a customer-managed key today; HSM-backed keys are an add-on for specific workflows. Monica — can you prepare the integration notes (key rotation, access policies) and a short diagram of the control-plane separation for the Private VPC offering?

- Network: we can publish a minimal egress IP set, and we support placing an inline inspection appliance in front of endpoints. I’m attaching our network-reqs-template to capture the specific CIDR and proxy details (Attachment stub below).

Proposed windows for the technical deep-dive (45–60m):
- Tue 01/12 10:30–11:30 PT (we can cover initial architecture + KMS integration)
- Wed 01/13 09:00–10:00 PT (alternate)
- Thu 01/14 15:00–16:00 PT (alternate)

If none of these work, propose 2 slots that do and we’ll accommodate.

Attachments: network-reqs-template.xlsx (Excel, fillable template)

Action items:
- Vivek: prepare compute isolation options and high-level BOM (lead time / cost delta).
- Monica: control plane separation diagram + KMS/HSM integration notes.
- Marissa: send calendar invite once Alice confirms a slot and share the Drive link for the architecture docs (HubSpot record attached for deal tracking).

Looking forward —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
